analysis.title: Partying Like It's 1999... In Coca-Cola: BofA Says Defensive Froth Is A Feature Of Bubble Markets
key_insights: BofA's Bubble Risk Indicator (BRI) is a price-based 0-to-1 gauge combining returns, vol, momentum and fragility. Readings above 0.8 are flagged as elevated bubble risk. As of Oct 23, US healthcare is at about 0.8, the highest of any asset BofA tracks, with staples at about 0.74 and energy at about 0.7.

Tech is around 0.5, the Nasdaq about 0.3 and the Mag7 about 0.25, so defensives show more bubble-like price action than the AI trade they were meant to hedge. BofA also says healthcare and staples read higher than Bitcoin, Ethereum and Kospi.

The rotation out of AI into healthcare and staples has pushed those sectors toward bubble-risk levels. BofA's 30-year sector heatmap shows the same pattern in the late-90s dotcom period and the post-COVID melt-up, when readings were elevated almost everywhere, defensives included.

BofA says structurally bubble-like markets can create frothy dynamics in sectors where fundamentals may not support them. It reads this as evidence that markets are moving toward an increasingly reflexive and boom-bust prone regime.
Froth is still localized. About 15 S&P 500 stocks have a BRI above 0.8, versus 50 to 100 at the dotcom peaks. Those 15 names are 2.2% of S&P market cap, versus 20% to 40% at the dotcom peaks.
Names with the highest BRI readings include MRNA, ZBRA, CRWD, IFF and RVTY, followed by KO, AMGN, CBOE and PANW.

BofA now publishes the BRI weekly and has extended it to equity themes. Cloud compute has the highest theme reading, followed by oil & gas and high dividend. The biggest one-week jumps were in high dividend, low vol and biotech.

Custom basket BRI readings: Brazil Election 0.94, US Cyber Security 0.92, US Software 0.76, Oil & Gas ex-Renewables 0.73, Pharma Hyperscalers 0.70, Japan Defensives 0.70. China Internet, Macau Gaming and China Anti-Involution baskets show essentially zero froth.

BofA's Global Financial Stress Index rose from +0.09 to +0.20 last week, its highest since April. Commodities and equities are the most stressed asset classes, crude implied vol stress is the highest since July 31, and European stress is above its long-run median. The GFSI Risk Allocator moved to a 4.9% underweight from neutral.

BofA treats a high BRI as a 'watch out' signal, not a 'get out' one. Historically, readings above 0.8 have come with more near-term downside risk but broadly similar upside, so the bank prefers adding asymmetric protection to outright selling.
BofA's trade from the prior week is a put-vs-put switch: buy XLP or XLV November puts and sell equal notional XLK November puts, for a small credit (0.23% and 0.20% respectively at the Oct 19 open).

The article's author (ZeroHedge, not BofA) adds that the next leg of the rotation may be about which bubble deflates first, and expects defensives to deflate. This is the author's view, not BofA's. The article also notes the Nasdaq fell nearly 3% over the past week.

tension_points.bull_case: Froth is still localized. Only about 15 S&P 500 stocks have a BRI above 0.8, versus 50 to 100 at the dotcom peaks, and they are 2.2% of index weight versus 20% to 40%. BofA says readings above 0.8 have come with broadly similar upside.
tension_points.bear_case: Readings above 0.8 have historically come with more near-term downside risk. Healthcare and staples now read higher than tech, and BofA sees the market moving toward a reflexive, boom-bust prone regime. Stress is at its highest since April.
